findings.finding: Using unit/record separators (`%x1d`, `%x1f`) in the git format string is sound and also fixes the existing `|`-in-subject field-shift bug — good catch. However, `%(trailers:key=...)` requires git ≥ 2.32 for the `key=` filter with `valueonly` semantics settling correctly; behavior is subtly broken on older gits (trailer key silently dropped).
findings.suggestion: Check the repo's minimum git version or fall back to parsing raw `%(trailers)` output; at minimum add the git version assumption as a comment/test-environment note.

findings.finding: Trailer values are free-form: a co-author can be `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` but could also be `claude-3.5-sonnet`, `GitHub Copilot`, or a human whose name contains "Claude". Matching "names Claude, case-insensitive" may over- or under-count.
findings.suggestion: Pin down the matching rule (e.g., case-insensitive substring "claude" in name or the anthropic noreply email), and document it. Also confirm the AI-author check still matches the existing author-name heuristic so the human-authored count doesn't regress for repos with Claude authors.

findings.finding: Multiple trailers per commit: the plan uses a separator but `unfold` and multi-line trailer values could still produce stray newlines; also `-z`-less `git log` splits records on newlines only.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the record separator scheme keeps each commit on one log line (e.g., strip CR/LF rather than `strip()` as noted, and test a commit with two co-author trailers and a subject containing `\n`-adjacent characters like pipes and unicode separators).

findings.finding: CommitEntry grows a defaulted field; positional constructors remain valid per the plan's own risk note. Fine — but if CommitEntry is serialized anywhere (caching, JSON report payloads), a new field may break older deserialization.
findings.suggestion: Verify CommitEntry isn't persisted/loaded; if it is, make deserialization tolerant of the missing field.

findings.finding: Empty/absent trailer: `%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,...)` yields an empty string, so splitting on the separator must skip empty segments, or you'll get a phantom empty co-author (harmless for Claude matching, but noisy for equality tests).
Reports already generated with the wrong counts (change-history.md showing 0/1868) — does regeneration happen automatically or is there a stale-cache/report regeneration step not covered by the plan?
findings.suggestion: Confirm the collector/report regeneration is triggered (spec's "Done when" mentions regeneration); add it to acceptance criteria.

findings.finding: The end-to-end test never asserts the parsed `co_authors` values themselves (e.g. that commit 3 has two co-authors, one of them Ada). A parser that dropped all but the first trailer would still pass.

findings.suggestion: If precision matters later, match on the name token or the noreply@anthropic.com address; not required by this spec. findings.finding: The diff updates the generator but omits the regenerated `.shipwright/compliance/change-history.md`. The scope explicitly requires the Shipwright report to show a nonzero AI-assisted count, and the fixture tests only establish that result for synthetic history.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the report against Shipwright’s history and include the updated artifact. Verify that the AI-assisted count is nonzero.

findings.finding: Git commit subjects can contain the control bytes used as delimiters. A subject containing `\x1f` produces six fields and raises `ValueError` at unpacking, aborting the entire collection. A subject containing `\x1e` splits the record and can cause the commit to be silently omitted.
findings.suggestion: Use NUL-delimited fields and records with fixed field counts. Add a fixture commit containing the current delimiter bytes and assert that collection preserves it and its attribution.

findings.finding: The classifier searches the entire trailer value, including the email address. A human co-author such as `Ada <ada@claude.example>` counts as AI-assisted even though the co-author’s name does not contain Claude.
findings.suggestion: Match against the co-author’s display name after removing any angle-bracketed email address. Add a test for a human name with `claude` only in the email.

findings.finding: The aggregate assertion checks how many commits were classified as AI-assisted without checking which ones. It can pass if a required trailer variant is missed and the plain human commit is incorrectly counted.
findings.suggestion: Assert attribution by commit subject for all four fixtures and verify that the two co-authors on the last fixture are parsed as separate values.  Ship-with-fixes. The approach fits the specification, but delimiter collisions can break collection, and the regenerated Shipwright report is still missing.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
